_about: Example configuration. Copy this file, edit it, and run:
Any key beginning with an underscore is a comment and is ignored. Every other key
must name a real parameter -- run --list-params to see all 56 with their ranges and
provenance. An unknown name raises rather than being skipped.
Values shown here are the shipped defaults, so running this file unedited reproduces
the standard output. Change the ones you know and delete the rest.
_1_prices: Start here. These are PRICE parameters -- organisational facts you already know,
and the cheapest thing to get right. SPEC.md section 8.
_2_portfolio: How many stories, by oracle closure rather than by size: can a machine decide
whether this is correct? Concurrent and ordering-sensitive code is Hard by
construction however well specified. SPEC.md section 2.
_3_measure_next: The four inputs to the escape equation, in the order the README recommends
replacing them. m comes free from one mutation-testing run (m = 1 - mutation
score); q_rev comes from the sampled-review stream and is emphatically not zero;
d is the failure rate of fresh implementations divided by the mutation score.
rho is NOT measured -- it is read off the menu in SPEC.md section 3.6 according to
how you have structured verification, and it is set per scenario below.
_4_human_time: Time-tracking on one instrumented epic. S is criteria-authoring hours per story,
R review hours per reviewed story, I hours to resolve one escaped defect.
Worth measuring: in scenarios C and D+, S is the second-largest source of
variance after escaped defects. SPEC.md section 5.
_5_scheduling: b is how many human touches you handle in one scheduled session. b = 1 means
every touch arrives as an interruption -- try it and see what it costs.
_6_reporting: FTE is quoted against this duration. It enters no cost. The saving this model
reports is a headcount reduction at roughly constant duration, not a speed-up.
_7_per_scenario: Per-scenario POLICY is addressed as scenario.parameter. The five scenario names
are execute_only, execute_decide, execute_deliver, all_three and
all_three_quality -- run --list-steps to see which process steps each activates.
These are the levers under discussion rather than things to measure.
_8_left_alone: Deliberately not set here: the correlation parameters lambda_e, lambda_f and
p_cluster. They are the hardest to fit and need several epics of history. Until
you have that, treat the defaults as structural assumptions and probe them with
--sensitivity lambda_e rather than editing them here. SPEC.md section 8.
